statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band as the recovery from Thursday's AI-led decline broadens into Europe with retracements intact, while Stress stays elevated on still-high long-end yields, unresolved energy geopolitics and wide dispersion inside the index.

The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the 13:30Z US cash open through 15:30Z, spanning the opening auction and the 14:00Z University of Michigan preliminary sentiment and inflation-expectations release. headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold the overnight recovery as oil and euro zone yields ease; Tail low, Stress elevated but easing
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed 8 October at 30,725.81, down 1.39%, after a Financial Times report that OpenAI's annualised revenue was roughly $20bn below previously indicated levels. The decline was concentrated rather than broad: the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 3.39%, Oracle lost more than 5%, Nvidia fell nearly 3% and AMD nearly 4%, while the Dow rose 0.1%. Three developments since have partly reversed it. Bloomberg reported that OpenAI expects annualised revenue to reach or exceed $70bn by year-end against a roughly $50bn run rate at the end of September, which counters the slowdown reading. In Tokyo, SoftBank fell as much as 7.3% intraday before closing near 4% lower, a clear retracement rather than compounding liquidation. In Europe, the STOXX 600 rose 0.9% to 630.83 by 08:41Z, recovering from a near four-month low, and euro zone yields eased after reaching multi-decade highs earlier in the week. NQ December futures trade at 31,225.75, up 0.83% from a 30,969.50 settle, inside a 30,953.00 to 31,266.50 overnight range and roughly 40 points below that high. Nvidia is bid near 234.41 in premarket against a 230.48 close, and VIX at 15.22 sits below its 15.41 prior close. The single amplifier present is proximity to the overnight extreme, and that extreme is a retracement of Thursday's decline rather than extension into new ground. Pullbacks are occurring at every level examined, so mean reversion is functioning rather than failing and Tail stays in the low band at 17. Stress eases one point to 47 but stays elevated rather than moderate for three reasons. Long-end Treasury yields remain historically high, with the 10-year at 5.28% and the 30-year at 5.67% on the 7 October H.15 observation and the 10-year quoted near 5.25% this morning. Energy geopolitics is unresolved: President Trump's statement that Washington will not strike Iran before the 3 November midterm elections pulled Brent down 1.3% to 102.91 and WTI 1.2% to 90.40, but Iran is reportedly reviewing a US response on reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, and Hurricane Isaias has shut in about 1.3 million barrels per day of Gulf of Mexico output. Third, dispersion inside the index is wide: European telecoms fell 3.4% to an eight-month low after SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide US low-band spectrum portfolio, with Deutsche Telekom down 8% and T-Mobile US down 7% in premarket, offsetting the semiconductor repair. Conflicting breadth of that kind reduces directional conviction and raises Stress; it does not mechanically raise Tail. Confidence is 88: current futures, index, volatility, yield, oil, European and Asian session evidence was verified directly, the seven-day US calendar was checked, and the shared Finviz context was unusable this run because its latest collection is dated 29 September and reports partial status, so it was excluded rather than treated as current. The scheduled checkpoints ahead are the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary sentiment and inflation-expectations release, the 20:00Z Friday cash close with the Fed Collins appearance, and next week's 14 October CPI and 15 October PPI and Retail Sales block.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours began in the watch band through the European and US sessions of 8 October and peaked at Tail 28 with Stress 72 in the 17:00Z slot, when the Financial Times report on OpenAI revenue drove the Nasdaq-100 to a 1.39% decline and the Philadelphia semiconductor index to -3.39%. Risk then eased steadily: Tail returned to the low band from 20:00Z and Stress fell from 72 to 49 by 08:00Z as futures recovered, oil reversed and implied volatility contracted.
outlookSummary: The low-Tail reading holds through the remaining European hours while the recovery keeps producing retracements. Tail enters the watch band across the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z Michigan preliminary release, peaking at 23 in the 14:00Z slot, then decays if post-release price discovery stays orderly. A second watch-band slot covers the 20:00Z Friday cash close and the scheduled Fed Collins appearance. From 21:00Z the CME equity index futures weekend halt removes NQ price discovery for the remaining twelve slots, where in-hour Tail sits at a structural floor and Confidence decays with distance from the last observed price.
